brief.meaningEn: Visible to others rather than kept hidden or confined to private thought.
brief.meaningZh: 讓其他人看得見，而不是藏起來或只留在心裏。
brief.grammar: The source applies the phrase to children openly showing imagination; it does not mean physically outdoors.
brief.register: Creative work, ideas and public sharing.
brief.boundaryZh: 公開呈現想法不等於要求分享每個私人念頭，也不保證所有人都同意。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把 open 誤作露天地方；重點是別人能看見表達。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出原本隱藏的內容、怎樣展示，以及誰能看見。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 87, row 2; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Children often show their imagination out in the open.

listening.promptZh: 學生怎樣公開表達想法？

options.en: They showed sketches and discussed them with classmates.
options.zh: 他們展示草圖並與同學討論。

options.en: They kept every drawing inside their private notebooks.
options.zh: 他們把所有圖畫留在私人筆記簿內。

options.en: They moved the workshop to an outdoor park.
options.zh: 他們把工作坊搬到戶外公園。

options.en: They let only the teacher see the sketches.
options.zh: 他們只讓教師看草圖。

listening.explanationZh: 共用展板與同學討論令想法可被看見。
listening.en: At a children’s design workshop, pupils pinned early sketches to a shared board and talked through the ideas with classmates. Their imagination was out in the open rather than hidden in private notebooks.
listening.zh: 在兒童設計工作坊，學生把初步草圖釘在共用展板上，並與同學討論想法。他們的想像力公開呈現，不再只藏於私人筆記簿。

reply.promptZh: （學生使用共用展板後有甚麼改變？）

options.en: Their draft ideas became visible to classmates.
options.zh: 同學可以看到他們的初步想法。

options.en: They could discuss sketches that had been private.
options.zh: 他們可以討論原本只在私人筆記裏的草圖。

options.en: Their imagination was out in the open.
options.zh: 他們的想像力公開呈現。

options.en: The board made their work available for feedback.
options.zh: 展板讓作品可以得到意見。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出想法由私人筆記轉為可供他人觀看和討論。
reply.promptEn: What changed when the pupils used the shared board?

scene.promptZh: 劇團把服裝初稿貼在排練室的共用牆上，演員可提出意見；草稿原本只存於設計師電腦。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The costume ideas are now out in the open for the cast to discuss.
options.zh: 服裝構思現在公開呈現，演員可以討論。

options.en: The cast can see the drafts, but only the designer may comment on them.
options.zh: 演員可以看到初稿，但只有設計師可以提出意見。

options.en: The shared wall displays only the finished costumes, not the draft ideas.
options.zh: 共用牆只展示已完成的服裝，而非初步構思。

scene.explanationZh: 從私人電腦轉到共用牆，構思可被演員看見及討論。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句誤把 open 當成「露天」？

options.en: A shared display can make ideas visible.
options.zh: 共用展示可讓想法被看見。

options.en: The phrase means the drawings have to be placed outside the building.
options.zh: 這片語表示圖畫必須放在建築物外面。

options.en: People can discuss a plan once it is no longer hidden.
options.zh: 計劃不再隱藏後，人們便可討論。

contrast.explanationZh: out in the open 在此指公開可見，與是否在戶外無關。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「初稿還在我的電腦，大家怎樣給意見？」你準備把它貼在團隊共用板上。哪句最完整？

options.en: Put the draft out in the open on the shared board so colleagues can see it and suggest changes, while keeping private notes separate.
options.zh: 把初稿放到共用板公開展示，讓同事看見並提出修改建議；私人筆記則另外保存。

options.en: The shared board is available.
options.zh: 共用板可以使用。

options.en: Colleagues may have suggestions.
options.zh: 同事可能有建議。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句指出展示渠道、可見對象和保留私人內容的界線。

speaking.en: The children put their designs out in the open on a shared board.
speaking.zh: 孩子把設計貼在共用展板上，公開呈現出來。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出誰可以看到那些設計。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區規劃小組原先只在內部檢視單車徑草案；現在把草圖放在公開會議的展板上，讓居民在修改前提出意見。用一至兩句英文描述改動。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出草案如何由內部文件轉成居民可見及可評論的內容；不要說最終路線已獲批准。

examples.en: The planning group put its draft cycle route out in the open at a public meeting, inviting residents to comment before revisions.
examples.zh: 規劃小組在公開會議展示單車徑草案，讓居民在修改前提出意見。

examples.en: With the route sketch out in the open on display boards, neighbours can review the proposal instead of guessing what the planners intend.
examples.zh: 路線草圖在展板上公開呈現後，街坊可以檢視提案，不必猜測規劃者的想法。

takeaways.en: An idea can be out in the open once its creator shares a draft.
takeaways.zh: 創作者分享初稿後，構思便可以公開呈現。

takeaways.en: The plan was out in the open for discussion, although no final decision had been made.
takeaways.zh: 計劃已公開供人討論，但尚未有最終決定。

notes: AI-authored provisional proposal; independent English, Chinese, media and browser QA remain pending.

lessons.titleZh: 幾乎不靠甚麼資源就做成

brief.meaningEn: Create something useful or enjoyable with very few materials or resources.
brief.meaningZh: 只用極少材料或資源，做出有用或有趣的東西。
brief.grammar: Out of introduces the scant materials used; almost does not mean literally no materials at all.
brief.register: Resourceful making, play and community projects.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調善用有限資源，不等於完全沒有成本，也不代表製作過程必然沒有時間、技巧或他人幫助。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把 almost nothing 說成完全沒有材料；重點是資源極少，而不只是花費很低。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出少量實際材料，以及如何善用它們做出成果。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 91, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: They made a game out of almost nothing.

options.en: A few simple items such as boxes, chalk and string.
options.zh: 少量簡單物品，例如箱子、粉筆和繩子。

options.en: An expensive set of sports equipment.
options.zh: 一套昂貴的運動器材。

options.en: No materials of any kind.
options.zh: 完全沒有任何材料。

options.en: A professionally built obstacle course.
options.zh: 專業建造的障礙賽道。

listening.explanationZh: 活動用了少量簡單材料，並非完全沒有材料。
listening.en: The youth club had only chalk, empty boxes and string for a rainy-day activity. The children made an indoor obstacle course out of almost nothing and spent the afternoon playing.
listening.zh: 青年中心為雨天活動只備有粉筆、空箱和繩子。孩子用這極少量的材料做成室內障礙賽道，玩了一個下午。

options.en: They turned simple supplies into a course.
options.zh: 他們用簡單用品做出賽道。

options.en: They used boxes and string creatively.
options.zh: 他們有創意地使用箱子和繩子。

options.en: They made an obstacle course out of almost nothing.
options.zh: 他們用極少材料做成障礙賽道。

options.en: They found a game in the few materials available.
options.zh: 他們善用手頭不多的材料做出遊戲。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明如何用少量材料創造活動。
reply.promptEn: How did the children make the afternoon enjoyable?

scene.promptZh: 學校樂隊只有幾個空罐和木匙，卻編出一段可在午膳表演的節奏。哪句最貼切？

options.en: They created a percussion piece out of almost nothing.
options.zh: 他們用極少材料創作一段敲擊樂。

options.en: They used the cans and spoons, but a teacher supplied the finished rhythm.
options.zh: 他們用了空罐和木匙，但整段節奏由老師編好。

options.en: The cans and spoons provided the sounds, but the group did not shape them into a performance.
options.zh: 空罐和木匙提供了聲音，但樂隊沒有用它們編成表演。

scene.explanationZh: 空罐和木匙是少量實際材料，可創作節奏。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把 almost 誤讀成「完全」？

options.en: A few reused items can still count as very limited resources.
options.zh: 幾件重用物品仍可算是資源極少。

options.en: The phrase means the maker used literally no materials at all.
options.zh: 這片語表示製作者真的完全沒有使用材料。

options.en: Time and skill may still be needed.
options.zh: 仍可能需要時間和技巧。

contrast.explanationZh: almost nothing 是強調材料少，不是字面上零材料。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「空罐和木匙也算材料，怎能說 out of almost nothing？」你知道樂隊沒有其他樂器。哪句最完整？

options.en: The band created a rhythm out of almost nothing: the few reused items were real materials, but they had no full set of instruments.
options.zh: 樂隊用極少材料創作節奏：幾件重用物品確是材料，但他們沒有整套樂器。

options.en: The band used some empty cans.
options.zh: 樂隊用了幾個空罐。

options.en: They did not have a full drum kit.
options.zh: 他們沒有整套鼓。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句保留少量材料的事實，也解釋誇張程度。

speaking.en: The club made an obstacle course out of almost nothing: just boxes, chalk and string.
speaking.zh: 青年中心用極少材料做成障礙賽道：只有箱子、粉筆和繩子。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出用到的三種材料。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區花園沒有預算買育苗盤，義工用紙盒和幾塊舊木板做成可重用的育苗架。用一至兩句英文描述他們如何善用資源。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出實際用到的少量重用材料，以及做出的用途；不要寫成完全沒有材料或不用工夫。

examples.en: The volunteers made a reusable seedling rack out of almost nothing, using paper cartons and a few old boards instead of new equipment.
examples.zh: 義工用紙盒和幾塊舊木板代替新設備，靠這極少量材料做成可重用的育苗架。

examples.en: With reused cartons and spare timber, the garden team built a seedling rack out of almost nothing, though it still took careful work.
examples.zh: 花園團隊用重用紙盒和剩餘木材做成育苗架，雖然材料極少，仍花了心思。

takeaways.en: With a little time, children can create a new pastime out of almost nothing.
takeaways.zh: 孩子只要有一點時間，就可以用極少材料創造新的消遣活動。

takeaways.en: The artists made a street display out of almost nothing, but they still planned it carefully.
takeaways.zh: 藝術家用極少材料做成街頭展覽，但仍仔細規劃。
